t: Answer; do not be confused or doubt anything: tell these gentlemen what happened, so that it may be seen and considered what good there is in the knights-errant I say there are on the roads.

o: — Todo lo que vuestra merced ha dicho es mucha verdad —respondió el muchacho—, pero el fin del negocio sucedió muy al revés de lo que vuestra merced se imagina.
t: "All that your worship has said is very true," the boy replied, "but the outcome of the business came about quite the reverse of what your worship imagines."

o: —replicó don Quijote—; luego, ¿no te pagó el villano?
t: "So then," said Don Quixote, "the villain did not pay you?"

o: En efeto: él me paró tal, que hasta ahora he estado curándome en un hospital del mal que el mal villano entonces me hizo.
t: In fact, he beat me so badly that until now I have been curing myself in a hospital from the harm that wicked villain did me then.

o: De todo lo cual tiene vuestra merced la culpa, porque si se fuera su camino adelante y no viniera donde no le llamaban, ni se entremetiera en negocios ajenos, mi amo se contentara con darme una o dos docenas de azotes, y luego me soltara y pagara cuanto me debía.
t: For all of which your worship is to blame, because if he had gone on his way and had not come where he was not called, nor meddled in other people's business, my master would have been content to give me a dozen or two of lashes, and then let me go and pay me what he owed me.

o: Mas, como vuestra merced le deshonró tan sin propósito y le dijo tantas villanías, encendiósele la cólera, y, como no la pudo vengar en vuestra merced, cuando se vio solo descargó sobre mí el nublado, de modo que me parece que no seré más hombre en toda mi vida.
t: But since your worship dishonored him so wantonly and told him so many villainies, his anger was kindled, and, since he could not take it out on your worship, when he found himself alone he poured it all on me, so that I think I shall never be a whole man again in all my life.

o: — El daño estuvo —dijo don Quijote— en irme yo de allí; que no me había de ir hasta dejarte pagado, porque bien debía yo de saber, por luengas experiencias, que no hay villano que guarde palabra que tiene, si él vee que no le está bien guardalla.
t: "The fault," said Don Quixote, "lay in my leaving there; for I should not have gone until I had paid you, since I ought to know well, from long experience, that there is no villain who keeps a word he has given, if he sees that keeping it does not suit him."

o: Pero ya te acuerdas, Andrés, que yo juré que si no te pagaba, que había de ir a buscarle, y que le había de hallar, aunque se escondiese en el vientre de la ballena.
t: But you remember, Andrés, that I swore that if he did not pay you I would go and seek him out, and would find him, even if he hid himself in the belly of a whale.

o: — Así es la verdad —dijo Andrés—, pero no aprovechó nada.
t: "That is the truth," said Andrés, "but he made nothing of it."

o: — Ahora verás si aprovecha —dijo don Quijote.
t: "Now you will see if he makes anything of it," said Don Quixote.

o: Y, diciendo esto, se levantó muy apriesa y mandó a Sancho que enfrenase a Rocinante, que estaba paciendo en tanto que ellos comían.
t: Saying this, he got up in a hurry and ordered Sancho to rein in Rocinante, who was grazing while they ate.

o: Preguntóle Dorotea qué era lo que hacer quería.
t: He asked Dorotea what it was she meant to do.

o: Él le respondió que quería ir a buscar al villano y castigalle de tan mal término, y hacer pagado a Andrés hasta el último maravedí, a despecho y pesar de cuantos villanos hubiese en el mundo.
t: She answered that she meant to go and find the villain and punish him for his foul conduct, and to make Andrés paid to the last maravedí, in spite of and against all the villains in the world.

o: A lo que ella respondió que advirtiese que no podía, conforme al don prometido, entremeterse en ninguna empresa hasta acabar la suya; y que, pues esto sabía él mejor que otro alguno, que sosegase el pecho hasta la vuelta de su reino.
t: To which she replied that he should take warning that, according to the gift he had promised, he could not take on any undertaking until his own was finished; and since he knew that better than anyone else, he should calm his heart until the return of his kingdom.

o: — Así es verdad —respondió don Quijote—, y es forzoso que Andrés tenga paciencia hasta la vuelta, como vos, señora, decís; que yo le torno a jurar y a prometer de nuevo de no parar hasta hacerle vengado y pagado.
t: "That is true," answered Don Quixote, "and Andrés must have patience until my return, as you say, madam; and I swear and promise him anew that I will not stop until he is avenged and paid."

o: — No me creo desos juramentos —dijo Andrés—; más quisiera tener agora con qué llegar a Sevilla que todas las venganzas del mundo: déme, si tiene ahí, algo que coma y lleve, y quédese con Dios su merced y todos los caballeros andantes; que tan bien andantes sean ellos para consigo como lo han sido para conmigo.
t: "I don't believe such oaths," said Andrés; "I'd rather have now something to get me to Seville than all the revenge in the world: give me, if you have it here, something to eat and take with me, and may your grace and all the knights-errant remain with God; may they fare as well with themselves as they have fared with me."

o: Sacó de su repuesto Sancho un pedazo de pan y otro de queso, y, dándoselo al mozo, le dijo.
t: Sancho took out of his pack a piece of bread and another of cheese and, handing them to the lad, said:

o: — Tomá, hermano Andrés, que a todos nos alcanza parte de vuestra desgracia.
t: "Here, brother Andrés; a share of your misfortune falls to all of us."

o: — Pues, ¿qué parte os alcanza a vos? —preguntó Andrés.
t: "Well, what share of it falls to you?" asked Andrés.

o: — Esta parte de queso y pan que os doy —respondió Sancho—, que Dios sabe si me ha de hacer falta o no; porque os hago saber, amigo, que los escuderos de los caballeros andantes estamos sujetos a mucha hambre y a mala ventura, y aun a otras cosas que se sienten mejor que se dicen.
t: "This share of bread and cheese that I give you," answered Sancho, "for God knows whether I shall need it or not; because I must tell you, friend, that the squires of knights-errant are subject to great hunger and ill fortune, and to other things besides that are better felt than told."

o: Andrés asió de su pan y queso, y, viendo que nadie le daba otra cosa, abajó su cabeza y tomó el camino en las manos, como suele decirse.
t: Andrés took hold of his bread and cheese and, seeing that no one gave him anything else, bowed his head and took to the road, as the saying goes.

o: Bien es verdad que, al partirse, dijo a don Quijote.
t: It is true that, as he took his leave, he said to Don Quixote:

o: — Por amor de Dios, señor caballero andante, que si otra vez me encontrare, aunque vea que me hacen pedazos, no me socorra ni ayude, sino déjeme con mi desgracia; que no será tanta, que no sea mayor la que me vendrá de su ayuda de vuestra merced, a quien Dios maldiga, y a todos cuantos caballeros andantes han nacido en el mundo.
t: "For the love of God, sir knight-errant, if you find me again, even if you see me being cut to pieces, do not succor me nor help me, but leave me with my misfortune; for it will not be so great as what will come to me from your grace's help, whom may God curse, and all the knights-errant that were ever born in the world."

o: Íbase a levantar don Quijote para castigalle, mas él se puso a correr de modo que ninguno se atrevió a seguille.
t: Don Quixote was getting up to punish him, but he began to run so fast that no one dared to follow him.

o: Quedó corridísimo don Quijote del cuento de Andrés, y fue menester que los demás tuviesen mucha cuenta con no reírse, por no acaballe de correr del todo.
t: Don Quixote was thoroughly embarrassed by Andrés's tale, and it was needful that the others took great care not to laugh, so as not to finish him off completely.
